entities.summary: The TOP500 project ranks and details the 500 most powerful non-distributed computer systems in the world. The project was started in 1993 and publishes an updated list of the supercomputers twice a year. The first of these updates always coincides with the International Supercomputing Conference in June, and the second is presented at the ACM/IEEE Supercomputing Conference in November. The project aims to provide a reliable basis for tracking and detecting trends in high-performance computing and bases rankings on HPL benchmarks, a portable implementation of the high-performance LINPACK benchmark written in Fortran for distributed-memory computers.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The TOP500 project has had a significant impact on high-performance computing, enabling researchers and scientists to track and compare the performance of supercomputers worldwide. This has driven innovation in fields such as climate modeling, materials science, and medicine.
